title: Family Bills, Shared Plans and AutoPay in India
metaDescription: Track household bills, shared streaming and cloud plans and UPI AutoPay mandates across the family, with each mandate tagged to the person who approved it.
h1: How can a family in India track shared plans, household bills and AutoPay in one place?
summary: Family money in India is spread across many phones: a shared cloud plan, a streaming login, electricity and broadband bills, school fees, and UPI AutoPay mandates that each person may have approved on their own phone. A manual tracker such as Essara lets one person list those costs with their cycle and renewal date, set a monthly budget and get reminders, without connecting any bank account.

sections.heading: Shared plans: what the family rules allow
paragraphs: Family sharing rules differ a lot, so check them before assuming a plan covers everyone. Apple's Family Sharing lets an organiser and up to five family members share services such as iCloud+, Apple Music and Apple TV without sharing one Apple Account. Google One lets the plan manager share storage with up to five family members. Google's help page describes 15 GB of personal storage for each member, then a shared pool, and says family sharing is not available on the 30 GB Lite plan. The family group must be run by an adult aged 18 or over, and members must live in the same country as the manager.

Netflix works differently. Its help centre describes extra member slots for people outside your household. The account owner pays for each slot, the extra member gets their own login and profile, and you need a Standard or Premium plan in the country where the account was set up. For people who live in the same home, that is not the mechanism to rely on.

sections.heading: Household bills that are not subscriptions
paragraphs: Electricity, broadband, phone, rent and school fees have the same tracking problem as subscriptions: they repeat, they vary, and nobody sees the whole total. Give each bill its own entry with the real cycle. A school that bills quarterly should be a quarterly entry, not a monthly guess. Essara's bill reminders and its 'Needs attention' view show what is due today or tomorrow, which helps when several people pay different bills from different accounts.

sections.heading: UPI AutoPay mandates on different phones
paragraphs: This is where families lose track. A mandate lives in the UPI app of the person who approved it, so a mandate your parent set up on their phone will not show in your app. In Google Pay, mandates sit in Live, Pending and Completed tabs, and a Pending request needs action from the person whose app it is in. Approving or changing a mandate needs that person's UPI PIN.

Ask each family member to open their own Autopay section once and send you the merchant, the amount, the frequency and the next debit date. Add each one to your tracker under the name of the person who approved it, for example 'Dad, electricity AutoPay', so you know whose phone to check when a debit surprises you.

sections.heading: When a relative holds the account
paragraphs: A subscription is usually cancelled from the account that pays for it, which is often not the account on the phone you are holding. Google Play asks you to sign in to the Google Account that holds the subscription, and suggests switching accounts if you cannot find it there. Apple says that if a family member's Apple Account appears on a receipt, only that person can cancel it.

For a mandate, the cancellation happens in the UPI app that approved it, with that person's UPI PIN. Google Play keeps access running until the end of the period already paid, so check the subscription again after the next billing date to confirm nothing renewed.

sections.heading: Tracking the household in Essara
paragraphs: Essara's feature list does not include family or shared accounts, so one person usually keeps the household list on their own account, and each subscription, bill and mandate is entered by hand. The gain is one timeline: the renewals for the next 30 days, a reminder before each one, and a monthly budget with a daily spending limit. Because nothing is imported, every entry depends on what someone adds.

steps.name: Collect the lists
steps.text: Ask each adult for their Google Play or Apple subscriptions and the Autopay section of their UPI app. Note the amount, cycle and next renewal date.

steps.name: Create the account
steps.text: Sign up at essara.space/signup, or install the Android app from Google Play. The same account works on Android and the web app.

steps.name: Add household bills
steps.text: Enter electricity, broadband, phone, rent and school fees with the real billing cycle for each.

steps.name: Add shared plans at your share
steps.text: Enter a shared cloud or streaming plan at what you pay, and put the full plan name in the entry so the arrangement is clear later.

steps.name: Add mandates by owner
steps.text: Enter each UPI AutoPay mandate, naming the person whose UPI app holds it.

steps.name: Check reminders and the budget
steps.text: Check the 30-day renewals timeline, confirm a reminder is set before each renewal, then set a monthly budget to see what is left and your daily spending limit.

steps.name: Scan the school or utility bill
steps.text: Use the receipt scanner for a fee or utility bill. It reads the merchant, total and date, and you review them before saving. The free plan includes 5 scans a month.

faqs.q: Can the whole family see one Essara list?
faqs.a: Essara's feature list does not include family or shared accounts. One person can keep the household list on their own account, which syncs across Android and the web app, and the others can be given the totals. Nothing in the listed features lets a second person open that same account.

faqs.q: Does Essara read our bank account or UPI AutoPay mandates automatically?
faqs.a: No. You add every mandate yourself. Essara never connects to your bank or UPI app, never reads SMS and never asks for your UPI PIN.

faqs.q: How do I see all the UPI AutoPay mandates in my family?
faqs.a: There is no single family list in one app. Each person checks the Autopay section of the UPI app they use, and the mandates are then entered in your tracker. Google Pay groups them in Live, Pending and Completed tabs.

faqs.q: Is Essara free for a family?
faqs.a: The free plan includes unlimited manual expense tracking, 3 months of history, 5 receipt scans a month and 5 subscription slots. A large household with many subscriptions may need a paid plan, which unlocks unlimited history, scans and tracking. Check essara.space/pricing for current prices.
